subject: Follow-up: Competitive TCO vs Hyperscalers + next tests
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: Competitive TCO vs Hyperscalers + next tests

Hi Susan / Peter —

Thanks again for the 30m discovery today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: document ingestion + retrieval-augmented generation for internal analytics (short prompts, many repeated prefixes).
- Current pain: unpredictable inference spend with hyperscaler endpoints and inconsistent latency during peak batch windows.
- Key asks: clear per-1M token economics, impact of batching/prefix caching on TCO, and a short test plan to validate cost & latency on real traffic.

Initial notes (high level)
- Redwood gives options: Hosted API for quick eval, Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or Private if you need VPC/isolation.
- For cost modeling we typically show three scenarios by cache hit rate (10%/50%/80%) and batching under typical concurrency. I attached a short spreadsheet with an example model.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscalers_1M_token_tco.xlsx (spreadsheet with assumptions and per-1M token comparisons)

Proposed next steps
1) Marissa to share a short TCO/assumption sheet (attached) with per-1M token numbers and simple formulas.
2) Acme to pick one representative prompt set (we recommend ~1k prompts that reflect expected prefix reuse). We can then run a 24–72 hour smoke to capture cache hit rates and latency.
3) We set up a short dedicated/hosted comparison: same model, same quantization profile, measure end-to-end p95 latency and cost delta.

Can you confirm the prompt set and whether you prefer Hosted API vs Dedicated for the initial smoke (we can do Hosted to start if you want zero infra setup)?

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call this week to walk through the spreadsheet.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Can you provide the per-1M token number broken down by: model family (Llama/Redwood-curated), quantization (FP16 vs 4-bit), and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated)? We need to show this to procurement.
- For caching: our workflows have a high degree of repeated prefixes (templates + system prompts). Do you have realistic hit-rate ranges you expect? Procurement will want conservative and optimistic numbers.
- Also, how do you account for networking/egress and additional infra costs for dedicated capacity?

We prefer Hosted API for the initial smoke to avoid infra paperwork, but if Dedicated materially lowers unit cost for our expected throughput we might move to Dedicated for the deep test.

Can Marissa share the assumptions in the attached spreadsheet as discrete scenarios (conservative/typical/optimistic)?

Thanks — Susan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive TCO vs Hyperscalers + next tests

Hi Susan / Peter —

Attached is the workbook with three scenario tabs (conservative / typical / optimistic). High-level bullets below — please treat these as assumptions we can adapt to your telemetry: 

Key unit economics (examples, per-1M tokens):
- Redwood (hosted, mixed-medium model, FP16): list price ~$35 per 1M tokens. Effective cost depends on cache hits and batching.
- Redwood (dedicated, reserved capacity): with a monthly commitment and a mixed workload we typically model $18–22 per 1M tokens (depends on commit and model weight / GPU mix).
- Hyperscaler A (managed LLM endpoint): ~$75–95 per 1M tokens for comparable throughput when using their managed service (higher unit cost driven by single-tenant overhead and less inference optimizations).
- Hyperscaler B (bring-your-own VM + model): raw infra for inference can be cheaper at peak utilization, but engineering + ops + autoscaling gaps drive hidden costs (we include a 20–30% ops tax in conservative TCO).

Cache hit-rate assumptions (impact on effective tokens):
- Conservative: 10% prefix cache hit -> effective billable tokens = 0.90 * raw tokens.
- Typical: 50% -> effective billable tokens = 0.50 * raw tokens.
- Optimistic: 80% -> effective billable tokens = 0.20 * raw tokens.

Batching / concurrency impact:
- Small prompts with batching across concurrent requests can reduce per-token latency and increase throughput efficiency. Typical production batching we model at 1.2–1.6x token-efficiency depending on request shape.

Example TCO (from sheet, simplified):
- Raw 1,000,000 tokens/month @ no cache -> Redwood hosted ~$35, Hyperscaler A ~$85.
- With 50% cache hit -> effective tokens 500k -> Redwood hosted ~$17.5, Hyperscaler A ~$42.5.
- Dedicated reserved example (higher commit): with 50% cache hit and batching optimizations -> ~$9–11 per effective 1M tokens equivalent (spread across commit).

Notes on networking / egress:
- Hosted: outbound egress to client networks is billed separately on cloud providers (we can show sample numbers; typically <5% of inference spend for most text workloads).
- Dedicated: if you host in your VPC we provide a breakdown of egress + infra; we'll include a conservative network charge line in the spreadsheet.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscalers_1M_token_tco.xlsx (three scenario tabs), acme-prefix-cache-test-plan.md (test plan template)

If this looks reasonable, next operational steps:
1) Acme picks the prompt set + upload link to a shared S3/GCS bucket (or we can accept a sample file via secure link).
2) We run a 48-hour hosted smoke using your prompts to measure real cache hit rates and p50/p95 latency.
3) Review results and decide whether a Dedicated evaluation (1–2 week soak) makes sense for TCO.

I put conservative/typical/optimistic columns in the workbook so procurement can show a range. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the sheet with your finance/procurement folks.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the detailed breakdown. A few follow-ups: 

- Can you call out the exact test inputs you'd like for the prefix cache run? We want to ensure we don't accidentally bias the hit rate upward.
- For the Hosted smoke: what's the expected latency SLO (p95) for the model family you're suggesting? Procurement is asking for p50/p95 numbers and typical concurrency.
- If we do the Dedicated follow-up, what's the minimum commit you model for the $18–22 per-1M tokens example?

Quick answers to the above would help us prep procurement and our infra team. We'll aim to drop a 1k-prompt sample into the shared GCS link by EOD tomorrow.

—Peter

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive TCO vs Hyperscalers + next tests

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Peter. Short answers / next steps: 

Test inputs (we recommend):
- 1,000 representative prompts (mix of short and medium length). Include 200 system/template prompts that represent common prefixes.
- Randomize order but keep timestamps to simulate real concurrency.
- Provide expected concurrency shape (e.g., 5–20 qps burst, baseline 2 qps) so we match batching conditions.

Latency SLO (hosted example we suggest):
- Typical p50: 50–80ms for short prompts on the suggested medium-weight model.
- Typical p95: 250–400ms depending on concurrency and model size. We'll instrument and report p50/p95 for the smoke.

Dedicated commit assumptions for the $18–22/1M example:
- This models a monthly reserved commit that maps to ~4–8 GPU months of sustained usage depending on model family. Exact commit depends on mix of requests and model weight; we'll give a specific proposal once we see your sample traffic (happy to model two commit buckets: 4 GPU-mo and 8 GPU-mo).

Operationally: please upload the prompt set to the Google bucket link in the shared doc (I pasted the HubSpot link below for the deal). Once we have the sample, Marissa will run the hosted 48-hour smoke and share a result deck + updated cost sheet.

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/deal/RDW-ACME-2026-03
Shared doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sample

I'll schedule a 30m post-smoke review for next week (tentative invite to follow). Thanks everyone — excited to get data rather than estimates.

Best,
Aditya Rao
